scenes.label: Meet the team
scenes.title: The Connection Lab
scenes.caption: The club tests an object helper on coloured drawings and outline sketches. It gets three of four coloured drawings right but only one of four outlines. Tara notices that one overall success count would hide a difference between the two kinds of material.
scenes.speech: The club tests an object helper on coloured drawings and outline sketches. It gets three of four coloured drawings right but only one of four outlines. Tara notices that one overall success count would hide a difference between the two kinds of material.

scenes.label: The problem
scenes.title: What changed?
scenes.caption: The teacher asks for correct, incorrect and total counts for each style. The training collection contains many coloured examples and very few outlines. That gap is a reason to investigate, not proof that the tool works equally well for everyone or that one drawing style is less valuable.

scenes.label: How it works
scenes.title: Follow the evidence
scenes.caption: Neel adds relevant checked outline examples and proposes fresh checks before wider use. People can review and correct the helper’s suggestions. This classroom capstone evaluates fictional objects, never children’s ability or worth. The team must be willing to revise the helper or stop using it when evidence is inadequate.

scenes.label: Your decision
scenes.title: Decide and explain
scenes.caption: Results differ by style, and outline examples are poorly represented in training. Compare the actions, then explain which evidence supports your decision.
scenes.speech: Results differ by style, and outline examples are poorly represented in training. Compare the actions, then explain which evidence supports your decision.
scenes.dialogue: What should happen before wider use?

scenes.label: What changes
scenes.title: Check the consequence
scenes.caption: Improve relevant coverage, test fresh examples from both styles and keep human review. Do not hide the poorer result inside one overall number.
scenes.speech: Improve relevant coverage, test fresh examples from both styles and keep human review. Do not hide the poorer result inside one overall number.
scenes.dialogue: Identify a representation gap in object examples.

scenes.label: Enter the lab
scenes.title: Investigate in the lab
scenes.caption: Investigate coverage across styles, then compare group results, then use, revise or stop. Test your plan, read feedback and try a changed case. Save evidence; explain one limitation.
scenes.speech: Investigate coverage across styles, then compare group results, then use, revise or stop. Test your plan, read feedback and try a changed case. Save evidence; explain one limitation.
scenes.dialogue: What can a group comparison reveal that one overall count hides?
